description:
Three honey sellers near a place, each with an address and a website.

Four directories hold a corner of the answer each — the USDA's local-food
listings, OpenStreetMap, Google Places and sellers' own Nostr listings — so
this asks all four at once, merges what agrees, checks that each website
still answers and ranks by evidence, completeness, agreement and distance.
`sources` says who answered; `verify` on a seller says what to check first.

A place that does not resolve, or a radius with nothing in it, is a
refusal and the fare goes back. The game is a race for honey; this is
where the real thing is.

count.description: How many sellers to name. 1–10; three by default.

dpop_token.description: Proof that the caller holds npub. Either the grant envelope that receive_npub_proof returned, or the raw JSON of a kind-27235 Nostr event signed by npub: content "", a `u` tag holding this tool's exact name from tools/list, created_at within 60 s of now, and a random `nonce` tag.

near.description: Where to look: a place name, a postal code, or 'lat,lon'. What the patron told you — never a guess from where the request came from.

npub.description: The patron's Nostr public key (npub1...). Tool fees are paid from this patron's balance; dpop_token proves the caller holds it.

radius_km.description: How far to look, to 100 km. Omitted means as far as it takes, to 100.

name: beesknees_find_honey
title: Find honey sellers
